issues.failure_explanation: The abstract lists 'norm and condition minimization in the two-norm, Frobenius norm and Schatten p-norms for p>2' and stable rank maximization and asserts all of them are NP hard with no PTAS. The body shows Frobenius-norm minimization is polynomial, and gives no PTAS-inapproximability result for Schatten p-norm minimization, Schatten p-norm (mixed) condition numbers, or p-stable rank (blank entries in Table t_intro).

failure_location.quote:
We show that these criteria 
are NP hard and do not admit polynomial time approximation schemes (PTAS).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the abstract to say NP hardness is shown for the listed criteria except Frobenius-norm minimization, and PTAS inapproximability only for the subset for which thresholds are derived.
issues.overall_effect: The summary of results overstates the paper's scope; no formal result is affected.
issues.title: Abstract claims NP hardness and PTAS inapproximability for all listed criteria, including ones the paper shows are polynomial or leaves open
issues.why_classification: Purely a scope statement; the body correctly delimits what is proved, so a wording correction resolves it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We make no assumptions on the dimensions $m$ and~$n$ of~$\ma$.

issues.failure_explanation: For a column submatrix with k columns the correct lower interlacing index is n-k+j (with zero singular values for indices beyond min{m,n}), not min{m,n}-k+j. Counterexample with m<n: A in R^{3x6} with columns e1,e1,e2,e2,e3,e3 and C=[e1,e1], k=2: the display claims sigma_3(A)<=sigma_2(C)=0, but sigma_3(A)=sqrt(2)>0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace min{m,n}-k+j by n-k+j with the convention sigma_i(A)=0 for i>min{m,n}.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed general fact is false when m<n. Lemmas l_inter and l_inter2 apply it only to full-column-rank C (m>=k), where the index coincides with the correct one, so no downstream result is affected.
issues.title: Interlacing inequality (e_inter) misindexed for m<n
issues.why_classification: Local correction of an index; every use of the inequality is in a regime where it is already correct.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
adopt the Turing model of computation, 

where inputs are rational numbers and the input size is measured in the number of bits.

In the reduced instance we set
$m = 3M$, $k=M$, and $b=1$. Clearly, constructing $\ma$ requires polynomial time.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper fixes a Turing model with rational inputs, but every reduction constructs A with entries 1/sqrt(3) (and later decision thresholds such as b=k^{1/p}, sqrt(k)), which are not rational and cannot be written in finitely many bits; hence the constructed object is not a valid instance of the stated decision problems and 'constructing A requires polynomial time' is unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Scale A by sqrt(3) (0/1 entries) and phrase the decision thresholds in terms of squared or p-th-power quantities (e.g. det(C^T C), ||C||_(p)^p, ||C^dagger||_(p)^p, sum of squared singular values) so that instances and thresholds are rational; the criteria are homogeneous so hardness transfers.
issues.overall_effect: All NP-hardness reductions use the same construction and inherit the model mismatch.
issues.title: Reduction matrix has irrational entries, violating the paper's rational-input Turing model
issues.why_classification: A routine rescaling and reformulation of thresholds restores validity with all conclusions intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
A PTAS is a polynomial
time algorithm such that for each $\epsilon>0$
 there exists a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation algorithm for minimization problems, and a $(1-\epsilon)$-approximation algorithm for maximization problems

In the reduced instance we set
$m = 3M$, $k=M$, and $b=1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The reduction sets k=M, so the hardness gap (2√2/3)^{1/M} → 1 as the X3C instance grows. For any fixed ε>0, a (1-ε)-approximation algorithm would only distinguish true from false X3C instances with M ≤ log(2√2/3)/log(1-ε), a constant; X3C with bounded M is solvable in polynomial time by exhaustive search. Hence a PTAS for S-optimality would not imply P=NP, and the 'Thus, no PTAS' inference is invalid. Excluding a PTAS requires a gap bounded away from 1 uniformly in k.

failure_location.quote:
It is NP hard to approximate S-optimality maximization within a factor of 
$(2\sqrt{2}/3)^{1/k}$. Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for S-optimality maximization.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either produce a k-independent constant gap for S-optimality (a new construction) or withdraw the 'no PTAS' conclusion and retain only the factor-(2√2/3)^{1/k} statement.
issues.overall_effect: The PTAS-inapproximability claim for S-optimality (Table t_intro, Contributions item 4, Section s_volume3) is unsupported; only the weaker k-dependent factor statement remains.
issues.title: S-optimality gap (2√2/3)^{1/k} tends to 1 with k and does not exclude a PTAS
issues.why_classification: The advertised guarantee type (PTAS inapproximability) is abandoned; no comparable version follows from the given argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Does $\ma$ have a submatrix $\mc\in\real^{m\times k}$ with 
$\|\mc^\dagger\|_F \le b$?
Let $\mc \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times k}$ with $\rank(\mc) = k$ and $\|\mc\ve_j\|_2=1$, $1\leq j\leq k$.

issues.failure_explanation: The decision problems in s_psnorm1 and s_condno1 do not require rank(C)=k, but Lemmas l_pinv and l_cond (which supply the 'X3C true iff optimal value attained' equivalence) assume rank(C)=k. Rank-deficient submatrices of the constructed A can have smaller pseudo-inverse norms than sqrt(k). Example: k=M=4, sets {1,2,3},{1,2,4},{3,5,6},{4,5,6},{7,8,9},{9,10,11} on S={1,...,12} (false instance since 12 is uncovered, rank(A)>=4). The first four columns are linearly dependent with Gram eigenvalues 2, 4/3, 2/3, 0, so ||C^dagger||_F^2 = 1/2+3/4+3/2 = 2.75 < 4 = k and kappa_F(C) = 2·sqrt(2.75) < 4 = k. Thus the decision problems with b=sqrt(k) (resp. b=k) answer 'yes' on a false X3C instance, and the reductions as written are not valid.

failure_location.quote: The proof for all the norms is the same as that of Theorem~\ref{t_voldec} but uses Lemma~\ref{l_pinv} instead.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the constraint rank(C)=k to the decision problems (or define the criteria as +infinity for rank-deficient C), consistent with the rank-k hypothesis already used in the definitions of volume and condition numbers, and note that then all lemmas apply.
issues.overall_effect: NP-hardness for Frobenius/Schatten-p pseudo-inverse norms and Frobenius/Schatten-p condition numbers, and the lower bounds in the pseudo-inverse and condition-number inapproximability proofs (which implicitly assume full column rank), are not established for the decision problems as formulated.
issues.title: Pseudo-inverse/condition-number decision problems admit rank-deficient submatrices, which can beat the 'optimal' value used in the reduction
issues.why_classification: A standard local condition restores every reduction and bound; the method, conclusions and scope survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We derive an inapproximability threshold of~$\sqrt{k+\tfrac{1}{4}}$.

In the reduced instance we set
$m = 3M$, $k=M$, and $b=1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof shows only that false instances have ||C^dagger||_F >= sqrt(k+1/4) versus sqrt(k) for true ones, a ratio sqrt(1+1/(4k)) → 1 as k=M grows. A (1+ε)-approximation for fixed ε distinguishes only instances with k ≤ 1/(4((1+ε)^2-1)), a constant, and X3C with bounded M is polynomially solvable. The conclusion 'no PTAS' therefore does not follow.

failure_location.quote:
It is NP hard to approximate Frobenius norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse within a factor of 
$\sqrt{1+\tfrac{1}{4k}}$. Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for Frobenius norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish a constant, k-independent multiplicative gap (new construction/analysis) or withdraw the 'no PTAS' conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: PTAS inapproximability of Frobenius-norm pseudo-inverse minimization (Table t_intro, Contributions item 4) is unsupported; only the k-dependent factor statement remains.

issues.failure_explanation: For q=p/2>1 the Schatten q-norm of a block diagonal matrix is (||A||_(q)^q+||B||_(q)^q)^{1/q}, not ||A||_(q)+||B||_(q) (which holds only for q=1); the claimed equality fails and the chain of inequalities breaks (in fact (a^q+b^q)^{1/q} <= a+b). The lemma's statement is false: for C=I_2, C_1=e_1, C_2=e_2 and p>2, ||C^dagger||_(p)^2 = 2^{2/p} < 2 = ||C_1^dagger||_(p)^2+||C_2^dagger||_(p)^2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the statement by the p-th power version ||C^dagger||_(p)^p >= ||C_1^dagger||_(p)^p + ||C_2^dagger||_(p)^p, which follows from the same pinching argument using ||diag(A,B)||_(q)^q = ||A||_(q)^q+||B||_(q)^q.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised p-norm bound for partitioned pseudo-inverses (Contributions item 6, Section s_partinv) is false. Theorem t_pi3 does not use it, so no hardness result is affected.
issues.title: Lemma l_pi1 is false: Schatten p-norm of block pseudo-inverse is not superadditive in squares for p>2
issues.why_classification: The lemma as stated must be replaced by a weaker (though closely comparable) statement; the fix is contained and nothing else depends on it.
